introduction: “Prayer need not be in words, but in thought and attitude … Words without love mean nothing.” The guide begins with what makes prayer prayer, then joins it to means and to work, to the hours of the day, to praying for others, and at the end to study, decision and action. Much of this is the common ground of praying people. Jesus forbids vain repetition and rises before day; the psalmist prays evening, morning and noon; Paul speaks of groanings that cannot be uttered and tells his friends to pray without ceasing; Nehemiah prays and sets a watch; the Qur’an says that hearts find rest in remembrance and that every thing hymns His praise; Herbert ends his sonnet at “something understood”. And much of it is contested. Amos and Tagore ask whether God wants the chanting at all; Spinoza and Emerson object to petition; James says we ask amiss; Shakespeare’s king and Mark Twain’s boy both find that a prayer cannot be faked.
questions: “Words without love mean nothing”, and yet obligatory prayer is revealed “as a reminder”. How do the readings relate the prayer one feels to the prayer one is asked to say?
Nehemiah prayed and set a watch; Moses was told to stop crying out and go forward. What do reading 3 and its companions say about the division of labour between prayer and means?
Tagore finds God with the tiller, and Amos has God despise the feast days. What would the guide say is lost if work wholly replaces worship?
Spinoza and Emerson reject prayer for particular things. Look at what is actually asked for in readings 13, 20 to 23 and 51 to 56. Which requests would survive their objection?
Daniel faces Jerusalem; the Qur’an says God’s countenance is wherever one turns. Why turn in a particular direction (26, 27)?
“Pray, decide, act” (76). How does the guide’s ending change the meaning of the many readings about praying day and night?

outside.why: “Words without love mean nothing.” Coleridge’s mariner learned it at great cost: he prayeth best, who loveth best all things both great and small.
Claudius on his knees, unable to mean it: my words fly up, my thoughts remain below; words without thoughts never to heaven go.
Jesus on prayer as mere speech: use not vain repetitions; they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.
Prayer is attitude as well as word, like the music of a song. Paul: we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession with groanings which cannot be uttered.
George Herbert’s sonnet heaps up images and ends without any: Church-bells beyond the stars heard, the soul’s blood, the land of spices; something understood.
“Prayer is like unto the spirit, and means are like unto the hand.” Nehemiah, building under threat: we made our prayer unto our God, and set a watch against them day and night.
At the Red Sea Moses cries out and is told: wherefore criest thou unto me? speak unto the children of Israel, that they go forward.

“Work and worship must go hand in hand.” Tagore goes further: leave this chanting and singing and telling of beads! He is there where the tiller is tilling the hard ground. If work can be worship, why keep the chanting?

Amos has God refuse worship that goes with injustice: I hate, I despise your feast days; take thou away from me the noise of thy songs; but let judgment run down as waters. What does prayer owe to conduct before it is prayer at all?
“Thou hast created me to know Thee and to worship Thee.” I created the jinn and humankind only that they might worship Me.
Prayer is “the Water of Life”. As the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O God.
The heart is a mirror covered with dust, cleansed by continual prayer. The Qur’an: nay, but that which they have earned is rust upon their hearts.
“The human heart finds no tranquility except through worship.” Thou hast made us for Thyself, and our hearts are restless till they rest in Thee.
The Qur’an says the same of the heart in one line: verily in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest.
Prayer and supplication are two wings. They that wait upon the Lord shall mount up with wings as eagles.
“Mayst thou ever be in a prayerful attitude.” Paul’s shortest counsel to a young church: pray without ceasing.
Nothing is more important. Tennyson’s dying Arthur: more things are wrought by prayer than this world dreams of.

Spinoza holds that he who loves God cannot endeavour that God should love him in return. On his view petition misunderstands what God is. What would be left of prayer if he were right, and is that remainder what reading 1 calls “thought and attitude”?
“The first thing to do is to acquire a thirst for Spirituality.” Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness.
A physician is to pray that means appear to rebuild the world’s ruins. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.
Supplicate and seek His nearness with the heart. Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you.
Nothing benefits but supplication, service, and servitude to others. Faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.
Hemmed in by anxieties, he could only repeat one prayer over and over. How long wilt thou forget me, O Lord? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me?
When depressed, go alone and ask. Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted in me? hope thou in God.
Is any among you afflicted? let him pray. Is any merry? let him sing psalms.
“Through His remembrance is every sick one healed.” The prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up.

Emerson called prayer that craves a particular commodity vicious, a kind of meanness and theft, and prayer as a means to a private end. The readings pray for healing and for means. How do they stand to his charge?

Supplication draws one near and illumines the spirit. In every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God; and the peace of God shall keep your hearts.
“Turn to the Holy Shrine”; one can turn from any clime. Solomon’s prayer provides for the stranger from a far country who shall come and pray toward this house.
The turning “has no nearness or remoteness”. Whithersoever ye turn, there is God’s countenance. Why does a religion that says so still give its people a direction to face?
In prayer one turns the face. Daniel, forbidden to pray, kneeled three times a day with his windows open toward Jerusalem.
Prayer and fasting are commanded from maturity. The Qur’an: establish worship. Lo! worship preserveth from lewdness and iniquity.
Obligatory prayer is “a reminder to His servants”. Israel’s daily recitation is commanded as a reminder too: when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.
‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s supplication each morning. In the morning, rising up a great while before day, Jesus went out into a solitary place, and there prayed.
Those who “rise from their beds at dawn out of longing”. My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O Lord.
At midnight and at dawn. When I remember thee upon my bed, and meditate on thee in the night watches.
“Neglect not praying … in the gloomy midnights.” He went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God.
At eventide and at dawn, and at all times. Evening, and morning, and at noon, will I pray, and cry aloud: and he shall hear my voice.
Pray “during all times”. He spake a parable unto them to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint.
A believing woman is told to give thanks and remember. Mary: my soul doth magnify the Lord, and my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour.
“Pray fervently and tearfully.” The publican would not lift up so much as his eyes, but smote upon his breast: God be merciful to me a sinner.
Chant prayers with melody. Singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.
Be diligent in prayer and “the gates of bestowal shall be opened”. Ask, and it shall be given you; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.
James adds the condition: ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts. Which askings do the readings encourage?
Show forth humility and need. Give us this day our daily bread.
Day and night with “the power of utter helplessness”. The widow of the parable wears down an unjust judge by her continual coming.
“I joined with you in communion” and prayed for you. Paul: I thank my God, making mention of thee always in my prayers.
“I will beseech and implore” on your behalf. Samuel to a people who had rejected his counsel: God forbid that I should sin against the Lord in ceasing to pray for you.
Pray one for another. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.
The prayer of each being is “according to the limit of his own existence”. The Qur’an: there is not a thing but hymneth His praise; but ye understand not their praise.
The Psalter ends by handing its praise to all creatures: let every thing that hath breath praise the Lord.
Keep to trade and business, and continually supplicate. Study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands.
They raised their hands and longed for these Days. Simeon, waiting for the consolation of Israel.
Purity of heart is the condition of feeling guidance. Huck Finn, trying to pray for what he does not want: you can’t pray a lie. I found that out.
Fasting and obligatory prayer are two pillars. When thou fastest, anoint thine head, and wash thy face.
Prayer and meditation are two activities, each needing the other. Mary kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart.
With prayer “must go also action and example”. Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, but he that doeth the will of my Father.
Steps: pray, decide, act with confidence. Nehemiah before the king: so I prayed to the God of heaven. And I said unto the king.

shortfall: Some twenty of the readings are single sentences from letters that repeat one counsel (remember God at dawn and eventide; supplicate day and night); they share the companions of their neighbours.
